criteria.name: Register match
criteria.reason: The all-caps button label follows the established pattern from LEM-009 and LEM-011, using consistent casing and a concrete verb appropriate for low-stakes navigation.

criteria.name: Humour boundary
criteria.reason: No humour is present in this low-stakes interface label, which is correct. The casual phrasing 'CHECK OUT' is conversational rather than joking.

criteria.name: Plain language calibration
criteria.reason: 'CHECK OUT MY POLICY' uses standard English without unnecessary translation, but 'my policy' is assumed context rather than explicitly named. For consistency with vocabulary guidance preferring 'the person's...name when known,' a reference to the actual policy name or a clearer object would strengthen this.

criteria.name: Direct address
criteria.reason: The interface presumably knows the policyholder's name or policy nickname (as in LEM-009 which uses the actual email), but the draft uses generic 'my policy' instead of addressing the person or naming their specific subject (e.g. pet, car, home).

criteria.name: Character budget
criteria.reason: No declared interface character limit is provided for this button/header string, so budget compliance cannot be assessed.

criteria.name: Action verb consistency
criteria.reason: 'Check out' is not one of the concrete, consistent action verbs seen in adjacent approved flows (get, finalize, unlock, review); it reads as a slogan-like phrase rather than naming the specific next action on the policy.

compliance.reason: The draft consists solely of a short interface/button label ('CHECK OUT MY POLICY') in all caps, consistent with mechanics for interface section headers/buttons. It contains no promise of outcome, no guarantee of claim payment, no removal of a disclaimer, no unsupported judgement claim about a customer, no contradiction of known policy, and no attributed quote or factual public claim requiring a source. As instructed, an isolated navigation or button label is not failed for lacking surrounding context, source, or disclaimer. No compliance prohibitions are triggered.
